system: You are an equity research assistant at a brokerage. Analysts use your summaries to decide quickly whether a news item matters for a specific stock. Accuracy matters more than completeness: never state anything the article does not support.
prompt:
Target stock: JPMorgan Chase (JPM)

<article>
HEADLINE: Several banks are trading at new 52-week highs today: BAC, BNS, C, DB, JPM, TD, UBS, WFC

BODY:
[No article body - headline only]
</article>

Instructions:
1. Classify how relevant the article is to JPM:
   - "primary": JPMorgan Chase is the main subject.
   - "secondary": JPMorgan Chase is one of several subjects, or a key driver of the story.
   - "peripheral": JPMorgan Chase is only mentioned in passing.
   - "none": JPMorgan Chase is not mentioned; any link would be your own inference.
2. Use only information stated in the article (headline + body). Do not add background knowledge,
   prices or context that is not in the text. If the body is missing or is generic boilerplate,
   rely on the headline and set "information_quality" to "limited".
3. Keep figures (prices, %, $ amounts, dates) exactly as written. Attribute analyst opinions,
   rumours and "sources say" reports as such.
4. Write for an investor in JPM: the event, the key numbers, and why it could matter for the stock.
   If relevance is "peripheral" or "none", say so plainly and cover only what concerns JPM
   (or, if nothing does, the market context in one sentence). Do not invent a connection.

Return only a JSON object with exactly these keys:
{
  "relevance": "primary" | "secondary" | "peripheral" | "none",
  "event_type": "earnings_guidance" | "analyst_action" | "m_and_a" | "regulatory_legal" | "product_business" | "macro_market" | "management_corporate" | "other",
  "summary": "<= 50 words, focused on JPM",
  "key_facts": ["<= 3 short facts, each <= 15 words, keep figures"],
  "sentiment_for_ticker": "positive" | "negative" | "neutral" | "mixed",
  "sentiment_rationale": "<= 20 words",
  "information_quality": "full" | "limited"
}
text:
{
  "relevance": "secondary",
  "event_type": "macro_market",
  "summary": "JPMorgan Chase (JPM) is listed among several banks—including BAC, BNS, C, DB, TD, UBS, WFC—trading at new 52-week highs today, per headline only.",
  "key_facts": [
    "JPM listed among banks hitting new 52-week highs",
    "Other banks included: BAC, BNS, C, DB, TD, UBS, WFC",
    "No specific price or percentage figures provided"
  ],
  "sentiment_for_ticker": "positive",
  "sentiment_rationale": "New 52-week high indicates positive price momentum for JPM shares.",
  "information_quality": "limited"
}
